quantity: Tables 3, 4 and 5 of ITU-R P.533-14 section 5.3
description: The three published tables the long-path reference frequencies need: the W, X and Y coefficients of the operational-MUF correction factor K (Table 3), the subsolar latitude for the middle of each month (Table 4), and the winter-anomaly factor at 60 degrees geographic latitude (Table 5).

provenance.recommendation: ITU-R P.533-14 (08/2019), Method for the prediction of the performance of HF circuits
tables: Table 3, Values of W, X and Y used for the determination of the correction factor K (section 5.3.1)
Table 4, Subsolar latitude for the middle of the month (section 5.3.2)
Table 5, Values of the winter-anomaly factor Aw, at 60 degrees geographic latitude used in the equation for fL (section 5.3.2)
provenance.pages: Tables 3 and 4 on page 18 and Table 5 on page 19 of R-REC-P.533-14-201908-I!!PDF-E.pdf
provenance.transcribed_from: Read cell by cell off the published recommendation text. Thirty numbers in total: six in Table 3, twelve in Table 4 and twenty-four in Table 5. The module that reads this file pins its sha256, so an edit to any cell that does not also edit that constant fails the suite.
provenance.reference_divergence: The pinned ITU reference build cd172be5 (MedianSkywaveFieldStrengthLong.c) carries Table 3 and Table 5 as C arrays and agrees with every cell here except one: its Table 5 Northern-hemisphere September entry is 0.00 where the published table prints 0.01. Its array is exactly antisymmetric under a six-month shift, which the published table is not. Table 4 has no counterpart in the reference at all, which computes a full solar declination instead of using the published mid-month approximation; see fL.ts deviation 1.

table_3.quantity: W, X and Y of equation (32)
table_3.note: Section 5.3.1: "The azimuth angle of the great-circle path is determined at the centre of the whole path; this angle is used to linearly interpolate the angle between the East-West and North-South values." The interpolation is linear in the angle, not in its cosine.

table_4.quantity: sx, the subsolar latitude for the middle of the month
table_4.note: Section 5.3.2: "The solar declination, delta, can be approximated by the subsolar latitude for the middle of the month (sx) from Table 4." Index 0 is January.

table_5.quantity: Aw, the winter-anomaly factor at 60 degrees geographic latitude
table_5.note: Section 5.3.2: Aw is "determined at the path midpoint, which is unity for geographic latitudes 0 to 30 degrees and at 90 degrees, and reaches the maximum values given in Table 5 at 60 degrees. The values at intermediate latitudes are determined through linear interpolation." The quantity that is unity outside the anomaly is the FACTOR (Aw + 1) of equation (33), not Aw itself; see fL.ts, which states why the sentence cannot be read the other way. Index 0 is January.
table_5.hemisphere: Selected by the sign of the path mid-point's geographic latitude; the equator counts as northern.
